entries.reason: an expansion out of a narrow format, whose rule Conversion.h prints: the pixel is multiplied by 255, and the pixels of a sub-byte row are big endian within the byte
entries.effect: each pixel of the row, read big endian - the low-indexed pixel in the high-order bits of the byte - times 255; the refusals are the release's own: a flag outside the set the header lists is kvImageUnknownFlagsBit, GetTempBufferSize does no work and answers zero, a NULL buffer is kvImageNullPointerArgument and a destination larger than the source is kvImageRoiLargerThanInputBuffer. A sub-byte source row is read packed, which is what the release does and what the header means by sub-byte scanlines being unsupported
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4, which writes the bit order and the multiplication out; the host's own vImage, compared byte for byte in tests/backports/host/vimageindexed; the release's own armv7 caches, which say which release first exports each name
